security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU write_mnstatus() in csr.c:5498 constructs a write mask (MNSTATUS_NMIE | MNSTATUS_MNPP | MNSTATUS_MNPV) that excludes MNSTATUS_MNPELP (bit 9). When Zicfilp is enabled, guest M-mode NMI handler writes to mnstatus.MNPELP are silently dropped — the field behaves as read-only despite the spec defining it as RW-H. The bit constant MNSTATUS_MNPELP is already defined in cpu_bits.h:715 but was never wired into the write path.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: CSR write mask missing newly-defined RW field; grep for 'mask.*MNSTATUS' in csr.c to find write_mnstatus() where MNSTATUS_MNPELP is absent from the mask expression at line 5498
security_spec.summary: mnstatus.MNPELP (Zicfilp ELP save/restore across M-mode NMI) is read-only in QEMU due to missing mask bit — guest CFI enforcement can be bypassed on NMI return because software cannot restore the previous ELP state
